svg.text: Common ReMeDi app UI for ReMeDi e-Sanjeevani and ReMeDi IoT · Channel-specific call handling in ReMeDi Cloud · Reference deployment: e-Sanjeevani (MoHFW / C-DAC)
TLS · OAuth2 client-credentials, time-bound tokens · per-integrator identity · request audit
Authenticates to integrator · pushes results + report files
Integrator onboarding, API keys · doctor / nurse / CHO accounts
Same core services and data model for both products — only the integration adapter differs
Structured clinical data · per-integrator access control
Role-based access · encrypted transport · audit trail
e-Sanjeevani channel: CHO / Doctor selects ReMeDi tests in e-Sanjeevani; results return to e-Sanjeevani in its own format.
IoT integrator authenticates with its issued credentials and obtains a time-bound access token.
Integrator submits a test request: patient demographics, required tests, health worker's registered phone and its own visit ID.
Request is routed via the channel adapter to core services and appears on the health worker's ReMeDi app worklist.
Health worker performs the tests with connected ReMeDi devices; readings are captured automatically.
Readings and report files (PDF / image / audio) are uploaded to ReMeDi Cloud and the visit is marked complete.
Result Delivery Service authenticates to the integrator's receiver and pushes results + reports, retrying until acknowledged.
Trust boundaries shown as dashed zones · separate credentials in each direction · result push carries only the integrator visit ID (no patient name)
